title: a fixed-length list of the wrong length
notes: Was the S0 of the group: PDL crashed while reporting the user's error, inside the error reporter, so nothing was left to fall back on and what reached the user instead was the raw pydantic `ValidationError` the reporter had been called to translate -- 76 lines, two chained tracebacks, 18 frames, ending in `KeyError: 'items'`, and `prog.pdl` named nowhere. The mechanism was two decisions of `analyze_errors` apart: the array arm decided it was looking at an array with `is_array`, which tested only `schema["type"] == "array"`, and then read `schema["items"]` unconditionally for every element. JSON Schema does not require the two to travel together. `RetryConfiguration.jitter` is `ExpressionFloatOrFloatFloat`, one alternative of which is a fixed-length pair and renders as `type: array` with `prefixItems`, `minItems`, `maxItems` and no `items` key at all; the union arm selected it as `found`, because it is the only member `is_array` accepts, and the subscript raised. `jitter: [1, 2]` is a valid program and `jitter: [1, 2, 3]` is not, which is the whole of the reproducer. What the golden now demonstrates: the crash is gone and so is the pydantic block that was chained ahead of it -- stderr is one diagnostic and nothing else, because `parse_dict` reaches its `PDLParseError` and `generate` prints it. The subscript was not merely guarded. A `prefixItems` schema is a **tuple**, fixed length with a type per position, so guarding alone would have answered a length error with silence; `analyze_list` reads `prefixItems`, `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems` as the three separate keywords they are, and `list_length_message` says that three items were written where two are allowed -- which is the same rule the leaked pydantic block carried (`Tuple should have at most 2 items after validation, not 3`), now in PDL's words and attached to a line. The subject is deliberately the *list* and not the field: `jitter:` is a number **or** a pair, the union arm picked the pair because it is the shape the user wrote, and "`jitter:` is a fixed-length list" would be a claim about the field that the alternative next to it contradicts. Location 2 and not 3 on the same reading as `E-SCHEMA-007`: `prog.pdl:3`, the block path `retry.jitter`, an excerpt and a caret on the third item, and no `:col` in the header, which INVENTORY 7.9/7.11 hold for a separate decision. Fix 3: `jitter: [1, 2]` is the user's own first two items, checked against the schema by `satisfies` before being offered and executed to exit 0. `hygiene_traceback_expected` is gone, which is what makes `test_no_traceback` assert rather than xfail on this entry. One further false complaint had to be removed to get here: `prefixItems` elements are `{"type": "number"}`, `json_types_convert` maps that to `float`, and `isinstance(1, float)` is `False`, so descending into the elements accused `jitter: [1, 2]` -- a program that runs -- of holding two things that are not numbers. `is_of_type` admits an integer where JSON Schema says `number`, which is the reading pydantic uses; it is a relaxation only and cannot make a new complaint appear.
